title: Quartic reductions and elliptic obstructions for perfect Euler bricks
summary: We show that the perfect Euler brick (perfect cuboid) problem is equivalent to the following elementary question: do there exist coprime integers $a, b, m, n$ such that the two expressions $(2(a^2-b^2)mn)^2 + ((a^2+b^2)(m^2-n^2))^2$ and $(4abmn)^2 + ((a^2+b^2)(m^2-n^2))^2$ are simultaneously perfect squares? Despite their near-identical structure (differing only in the first summand), no solution has ever been found.
